newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends flat in sideways trade, data eyed.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends flat in sideways trade, data eyed.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures ended flat to firmer, quietly consolidating Tuesday's steep losses ahead of the weekly inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute, due after the session's close.
July crude settled unchanged at $20.79 a barrel after dropping 84 cents Tuesday.
July unleaded gasoline gained 0.04 cent to end the day at 63.04 cents a gallon. July heating oil rose 0.09 cent to 55.31 cents.
Wednesday's inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute was expected to offer little direction to the market, traders said, as figures were anticipated to show only mild changes.
Slightly higher inventories were seen for crude oil and distillates, while unleaded gasoline stocks and refinery capacity utilization rates were expected to be little changed to slight lower.
With capacity utilization rates at or near last week's strong rate of 97.6 percent, gasoline supplies were expected to remain healthy.
Although that prediction implies steady demand for crude oil, it could be bearish for gasoline futures, where traders are hoping to see some of the demand levels typical in the summer driving season.
If the API report shows a draw on gasoline stocks depsite high utilization rates, the overall complex could expect a mildly bullish reaction, traders said.
"The concensus is for a gas build, so any draw would be supportive" for the complex, said Al Lindseth at GSC Energy.

On the technical side, traders said crude oil futures could find some initiative to go higher after Tuesday's session low of $20.65, basis July, was successfully defended both during Tuesday's washout and again on Wednesday.
July will find intermediate support at the $20.65 mark, with more buying seen supporting values down to $20.50.
